title: Close the tenant-to-platform permission escapes and restore the tenant smoke signal
goal: A delivery audit of pantheon-base after the tenant remediation found three blockers: (1) the permission policy console ran the unbound service and took the target tenant from the request body, so a tenant administrator could create GLOBAL Casbin policies for its own role key, write into another tenant's domain, and list/export every tenant's policies; (2) role keys had no reserved namespace, so a tenant could create role_key=admin or platform_ops and inherit the platform Casbin/global grants at login; (3) Tenant Smoke (multi-mode advisory) was red on main because platform.tenant_mode was seeded non-public and Bootstrap never repaired an existing row, so the frontend hid the tenant controls. This task fixes all three, repairs the role-policy lifecycle (delete/rename/purge), makes the tenant-mode flag public and self-healing, and pins every boundary with two-tenant MySQL-backed tests.
findings: P0: permission_handler.go called h.service (unbound) for ListPolicies/CreatePolicy/UpdatePolicy/DeletePolicy/BatchDelete/ImportPolicies/ExportPolicies, so the tenant context was dropped and the service behaved as platform scope (isPlatformScope == true, ensureRoleKeyExists unscoped).

P0: PermissionPolicyCreateReq/UpdateReq carried tenantId from the JSON body straight into resolvePolicySubject; tenantId=0 produced a global policy for the tenant's own role key, which CasbinDomainPolicySubjects consults for every tenant, and tenantId=<other> wrote into that tenant's domain for a shared role key (tenant_admin).

P0: ImportPolicies and the workbench remediation wrote the bare role key as V0, i.e. a global policy, from a tenant-scoped request; requiredAPIRoutesByPermission includes system:tenant:list/create/update/delete, and subjectHasPlatformCapability treats any global policy for the routed path as platform capability.

P0: role creation only checked per-tenant uniqueness; a tenant could create role_key=admin or platform_ops. Login loads role keys verbatim from system_role.role_key, Casbin consults the global subject of the same name first, and PlatformCapabilityMiddleware admits platform_ops by name.

P1: deleteRoleBindings removed only v0=roleKey, leaving role:<key>@tenant:<id> policies behind so a recreated role key inherited the old grants; role renames did not move the policies at all (silent loss of API access).

P1: PermissionService.Bootstrap deleted every policy whose v0 was not a bare live role_key — which is every tenant-domain subject — on each boot, so tenant-configured policies were reverted to the default wildcard.
P1: the role CSV import created SystemRole without TenantID, so a tenant import wrote a platform-global role (tenant_id = 0).

P1: validateImportRoleKeys counted roles by bare role_key across every tenant; the bootstrap admin lookup (ensureAdminRoleBinding / ensureAdminUserBinding) also matched a tenant-owned role keyed admin.

P1: platform.tenant_mode was seeded with isPublic=0 while the Go fallback said 1, and bootstrapSettingSeed only inserts missing keys, so upgraded deployments never published the flag; the frontend gates the tenant picker/switcher/viewpoint switcher on it (AppLayout.tsx:1804-1805). Tenant Smoke failed at tenant-viewpoint-switcher.spec.ts:179 on every main commit since 8ffb00bf, masked by continue-on-error.
P2: the permission package fixture omitted system_role.tenant_id, which is why the unscoped behaviour looked correct in tests.

in: backend/modules/system/iam/permission/permission_handler.go (bind every policy surface to the request tenant)
backend/modules/system/iam/role/role_service.go (policy cleanup on delete, subject migration on rename)
frontend i18n resources (role.key.reserved in five languages)
two-tenant regression tests for the policy console and role lifecycle
out: Changing the Casbin domain model or the platform-capability definition (contract §4/§3.4)
Adding tenant-customisable menus or permissions (frozen decision 2026-10-15)
Backfilling existing tenant rows that already carry a reserved role key (operator runbook item)

implementationNotes: The tenant of a policy write now comes from the resolved request context. Tenant scope forces role:<key>@tenant:<ctx>; a body tenantId that disagrees is rejected with TENANT_FORBIDDEN. Platform scope keeps the explicit-target behaviour.
Reads (list/export/workbench) resolve the caller's role keys to domain subjects and filter on those; global rows are platform state and are not visible to a tenant subject (contract §2.3.1).
Import and workbench remediation compute the stored subject before writing, so a tenant row can never become a global policy. Role keys are validated inside the target namespace.
Reserved role keys are any key owned by the platform namespace (tenant 0) plus platform_ops. This is a namespace guard, not a per-tenant allowlist: tenant_admin/tenant_member remain usable.

Role deletion removes exactly the role's own subject; renaming moves p rows from the old subject to the new one. The bootstrap purge now recognises the domain form, so tenant-configured policies survive a restart.
platform.tenant_mode becomes public in the seed and Bootstrap raises is_public on an existing row; it never lowers it, so an operator-exposed key is not hidden.
No schema change to system_role/system_role_permission/system_role_menu. The only DDL is permission_workbench_remediation_event.tenant_id (migration 000028), guarded and idempotent.

commands: cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./modules/system/...
runtimeEvidence: Two-tenant MySQL tests prove a tenant-scoped create stores role:<key>@tenant:<id>, rejects a foreign tenantId, cannot read or export the other tenant's policy, imports into its own domain, and remediates only its own domain.
Role tests prove admin/platform_ops are rejected, deletion removes only the domain subject (the platform admin policy survives), rename moves the policy, and CSV import stamps the tenant.
Bootstrap test proves a live tenant-domain policy survives the orphan purge while a role-less subject is removed.
Tenant Smoke is the only browser-level proof that the public flag renders the switcher; it can only run in CI (this host cannot spawn a browser).

humanGates: Existing tenants that already created a reserved role key (admin/platform_ops) must be remediated by an operator: rename the role and delete its Casbin policies. This packet blocks new ones but does not auto-rename live rows.
Whether Tenant Smoke should leave continue-on-error after this fix is a maintainer decision; the packet only makes the job green.
completionChecklist: Every policy surface is bound to the request tenant and the body cannot choose the namespace
Reserved platform role keys are rejected in tenant scope and CSV import stays tenant-owned
Role delete/rename and the bootstrap purge handle the tenant-domain subject form
platform.tenant_mode is public in the seed and repaired on bootstrap
Two-tenant regression tests cover create/list/export/import/remediation and the role lifecycle
Full backend suite, frontend typecheck and repo gates pass
